result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both drafts make the same core case: fast actions update in place without blocking, and export gets its own non-blocking progress UI. B is more concrete on the cases that matter most. It explicitly reverts a failed optimistic rename, lets the user leave the editor during export, delays the indicator for quick exports, and uses a browser notification so the finished file is easy to find. A is solid but organizes its tiers less consistently, and it spends extra length explaining what's wrong before it gets to the fix. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B organizes its proposal around explicit duration bands (very short, ongoing, long) and suggests a duration-class status model, which directly answers the 'loading is loading' claim. A covers the same ground per action and adds good details like the 300–500ms delay, an export snapshot and optimistic revert, but it frames the advice less clearly around time. A is somewhat tighter, while B's extra sections push it toward lecture length.
